events.title: Nat at Night
events.description: On Fridays, the San Diego Natural History Museum is open until 11 PM just for you. Enjoy access to all open exhibitions and our rooftop deck for good views and great vibes. The rooftop is open to all visitors and serves beer, wine, non-alcoholic drinks , and food from Wolf in the Woods. Take a selfie with a megalodon shark, see scientists at work in our Paleo Center , admire glittering gems, get a close up look at spiders and snakes, and so much more. Best of all, get a look at our brand-new exhibition, Washed Ashore: Art to Save the Sea and grab a drink in the dive bar while chatting with a scientist. On select dates, channel your inner artist with Sketchparty , get competitive during trivia, or unwind while listening to the rooftop DJ. Hungry for more? The Craft Taco , located inside the Atrium, is a vibrant taco restaurant offering a delectable fusion of flavors and artisanal creations. They offer made-to-order tacos featuring signature blue corn tortillas, delectable burritos and bowls, and a variety of drinks and coffees. Admission is half-price after 5 PM, and parking is free after 6 PM. You can buy your tickets online in advance or buy them at the door the night of . As always, members of The Nat and Explorer pass holders enjoy free general admission.
events.location: San Diego Natural History Museum (The Nat), 1788 El Prado, Balboa Park, San Diego, CA

events.title: Knot Together
events.description: Inspired by the traditional fishing nets and nautical knots featured in To Catch a Fish , our newest Together workshop series, Knot Together , explores the art of macramé. The series is led by Sitoë Thiam, a fiber artist and mechanical engineer who bridges technical precision with organic expression. As the founder of Unknot, a design studio specializing in knotting and weaving, she brings a unique interdisciplinary perspective to the world of fiber arts. Knotted Rope Wall Hanging In September, learn to transform rope into a sculptural wall hanging. You’ll explore four foundational knots, building a rhythmic, colorful composition that celebrates the tactile beauty of fiber. The Together series at Mingei invites makers of all skill levels to come together and create in a supportive, low-pressure environment. Past iterations— Sew Together, Weave Together , Dye Together , Stitch Together , and Clay Together —explore a variety of craft techniques while emphasizing collaboration, experimentation, and hands-on learning. Each workshop encourages participants to connect with materials, try new skills, and enjoy the process of making together.

events.title: The Flight of Jackie Cochran Documentary Screening
events.description: Documentary Screening at the San Diego Air & Space Museum Friday, September 25, 2026 1:00 p.m. Pavilion of Flight Discover the remarkable story of one of aviation’s most accomplished—and often overlooked—pioneers during a special screening of The Flight of Jackie Cochran at the San Diego Air & Space Museum. The documentary will be presented on the Museum’s state-of-the-art LED video wall in the Pavilion of Flight. About the Documentary The Flight of Jackie Cochran tells the story of “the most famous pilot you’ve never heard of”—a woman who shattered aviation records, broke the sound barrier and helped change the course of history, only to be largely forgotten by it. A contemporary and rival of Amelia Earhart, Jackie Cochran became one of the most influential figures in American aviation. During World War II, she played a central role in establishing the Women Airforce Service Pilots, better known as the WASP, and later set an extraordinary number of speed, distance and altitude records. Behind Cochran’s public achievements, however, was a private life carefully constructed to conceal her past. Drawing on newly discovered archival materials and personal correspondence, the documentary explores a long-buried secret from her childhood and examines how her beginnings shaped her ambition, determination and relentless drive to succeed. The film also features scenes from the stage play The Flight of Jackie Cochran , written by and starring Nancy Hasty. Based on archival material uncovered during Hasty’s research, these dramatic reenactments bring Cochran’s voice and inner world to life while connecting her personal struggles with her historic accomplishments. More than a traditional biography, The Flight of Jackie Cochran examines how history chooses its heroes and why some extraordinary stories fade from public memory. It is a powerful exploration of ambition, perseverance, identity and the cost of greatness. Admission The screening is included with general Museum admission and is free for: San Diego Air & Space Museum Members Balboa Park Explorer Pass holders Seating is available on a first-come, first-served basis.
events.location: San Diego Air and Space Museum, 2001 Pan American Plaza, San Diego, CA

events.title: Kintsugi Workshop
events.description: In this hands-on workshop, guests are invited to bring a broken plate and learn the traditional Japanese art of kintsugi , the practice of repairing ceramics with gold. Guided by Japanese Friendship Garden & Museum staff, participants will carefully reassemble their piece while learning the philosophy behind this centuries-old technique. Kintsugi teaches us to see beauty in imperfection and to honor an object’s history rather than hide its flaws. By repairing what is broken, we celebrate resilience, transformation, and mindful making. No prior experience is necessary. This workshop is open to beginners and curious makers alike. The guest can practice on the small sauce dish that we provide before working on their own precious piece. To ensure a safe and successful experience for everyone, please follow these guidelines when selecting your plate: Guests will bring one broken plate The plate must be broken into no more than 5 pieces Maximum size: 12 inches (length) × 12 inches (width) × 4 inches (height) Plates should be clean and dry Please do not bring pieces with sharp shards or missing fragments Please bring a facemask if you are sensitive to the smell of glue All repair materials and tools will be provided. JFGM staff will assist throughout the process. Date: 9/26 Time: 10:00am-12:30pm Location: Education Center JFGM Member $80 | Non Member $100 *Admission to the garden is included. *Registration required. Refunds will not be given less than 7 days before the program.
events.location: Japanese Friendship Garden & Museum, Education Center, Balboa Park, San Diego

events.title: Book Launch: The Zoo Lady by Dr. Sandra E. Bonura
events.description: The Zoo Lady: The Forgotten Legend Who Saved & Then Built The San Diego Zoo She was a middle-aged, divorced mother who became the world’s first female zoo director and the first woman to lead the National Zoo Association (AZA)—so why has history forgotten her name? While Harry Wegeforth was the founder, it was Belle Benchley who ensured the San Diego Zoo survived its darkest days. In 1925, she took a temporary bookkeeping job at the struggling four-year-old zoo—a position she admittedly ‘dreaded’—only to stay for thirty years. She didn’t just save a failing institution; she built it into a world-class treasure, reshaping global conservation long before Jane Goodall or Dian Fossey. From wrestling rattlesnakes to orchestrating the historic cross-country giraffe trek that inspired the bestseller West with Giraffes, Benchley was a “leader of steel” who broke the glass ceiling. Join award-winning author and historian Dr. Sandra E. Bonura for a journey through rare archival images as she uncovers how this unlikely pioneer transformed a struggling local park into a global icon. Book Signing & Special Offer: Copies of Dr. Bonura’s brand-new book, The Zoo Lady: How Belle Benchley Built the San Diego Zoo, will be autographed and available for purchase at a special author’s discount. Program ticket includes lunch
events.location: San Diego History Center, 1649 El Prado, Suite #3, San Diego, CA

events.title: Meteorites as Artistic Matter
events.description: Speakers: Ulrike Arnold , Artist; Gerard van Belle, PhD , Former Director of Science at Lowell Observatory; and Rachel Jans, PhD , Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art at The San Diego Museum of Art MOPA@SDMA Joan and Irwin Jacobs Theater   Meteorites as Artistic Matter brings together internationally acclaimed artist Ulrike Arnold, astronomer Gerard van Belle, and the Museum’s Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art Rachel Jans, PhD, for a fascinating interdisciplinary conversation exploring the intersection of art, science, and the cosmos. Known for incorporating meteorite dust and pigments gathered from some of the world’s most remote landscapes into her paintings, Arnold will discuss how celestial and earthly materials become powerful artistic media. Joined by van Belle’s astronomical perspective and Jans’s expertise on the work of Sigmar Polke, a German artist also known for incorporating unconventional materials into his work, and contemporary artistic practice, this engaging guest lecture offers a rare opportunity to discover how meteorites inspire creativity, expand our understanding of materiality, and connect artistic expression with the vast universe beyond our planet. Following the lecture, guests are invited to enjoy a guided tour led by our docent team.   Please note, this lecture is in-person only and held at the MOPA@SDMA Joan and Irwin Jacobs Theater in Balboa Park. $15 members and students | $20 seniors and military | $30 nonmembers This lecture is presented as a part of the Guest Lecture Series , which offers a platform for renowned scholars and experts from the art world to share their insights and knowledge on topics related to art history, art theory, and the museum’s collections.

events.title: Skate Craft: Do-It-Yourself Design in Skateboarding
events.description: Celebrate skateboarding's true "Do It Yourself" ethos, from the boards, gear, and ramps, to the machines and the repurposed boards as objects of use. To land a trick, to make the make—that moment is everything. It’s the struggle between you and the skateboard, the challenge of turning something sketchy into a clean run. Whether it's mastering a carve, dropping in, or landing a trick, the average number of attempts is 10,000. When you finally achieve it, that's when it becomes a true "MAKE." This exhibition celebrates skateboarding's true "Do It Yourself" ethos, tracing its evolution from the early days of making decks in garages and building ramps from found lumber to the handcrafted works of art seen today. Experience how skateboarding nurtures creativity, self-expression, and joy through artisanal craftsmanship. The progression of skateboard design, safety gear, and skate shoes, alongside the inventive machines that facilitated their creation, is driven by a DIY ethos. Around the world, artists embrace this spirit by turning old skateboards into jewelry and furniture, demonstrating how skateboarding combines play, design, and sustainability in vibrant ways.
events.location: Mingei International Museum, 1439 El Prado, San Diego, CA
